status: Private execution contract recorded before implementation/evaluation; no live/provider/public/product/owner admission
composition: A separately compiled injected-reader probe retains its serialized InventorySession while the existing Windows GUI/TUI/linear shell runs. Initial mixed capture is prepared and actually retired before entry. An explicit optional application advance_observations callback runs on the same host thread before cached model observation and separately from operation CompletionPoll/tick. The shipped Fake composition supplies no callback and retains its current behavior. There are no producer threads, public flags or automatic live discovery.
delivery: Each model observe() obtains the service's prepared cached snapshot; unchanged pointers return false without modifying view state. Changed snapshots preserve exact evidence focus/selection, editors, typed parameters, request IDs, existing results and staged/reviewed revision. GUI/TUI advance their view epoch so later operation completions remain bound to the earlier view. Shell closes an open target chooser on delivery, without altering its editor, and preserves exact command/completion candidates and a reviewed request's original revision. It records one bounded observations-updated entry per delivered snapshot using existing transcript limits. Native getters and model tick never advance readers.
host_lifecycle: An optional before_model_release callback records the still-live model on normal loop return before its owner destroys it. It does not imply successful console restoration or reader retirement. Failed/early host entry can lack that final sample and must be labelled unavailable; actual controller observations remain separately retained. The ordinary product supplies neither callback.
stale_review: A review staged before a changed graph retains its original expected revision; submitting it follows the existing shared revision-conflict outcome before target lookup or health dispatch. Refresh/delivery never silently grants a new revision or rebinds an evidence ID to another row with the same name. A selected removed observation stays that ID with missing state.
scheduling: The private driver accepts at most three authored captures including the initial complete capture. Ordinary owned controller events request starting the next capture, releasing prepared readers, cancelling or timing out current readers. Pulses poll/retire with zero wait, publish only prepared immutable data, and preserve old publications on failure. Each running attempt has a finite 5000-ms observation deadline, with timeout recorded once and actual retirement still separately observed. No event permits replacement while the prior source remains outstanding. Signals are test workload controls, not authority or storage commands.
events: Exactly four distinct controller-owned auto-reset named events have names Local\DiskEd.Inventory.<32 lowercase hex nonce>.<advance|release|cancel|timeout>. The probe opens only those declared names and owns its opened handles. They add no remote endpoint, foreground input or global setting. Inputs and a new structured receipt use the existing bounded ordinary-file launcher profile. The GUI uses an owned inactive desktop; consoles use an owned hidden console. Structured evidence is separate from the actual frontend's visual/text display.
startup_barrier: The existing native reader's 1000-ms release barrier remains unchanged. Controller scenarios release within that budget, or deliberately record its unavailable/exit result; a requested gate never extends an existing native budget. The 5000-ms driver deadline is an outer observation bound, not a guarantee that a reader stays prepared that long.
failure: Start/publication/poll exceptions are recorded by the private application driver, leave published owners intact and remain failed/unresolved evidence. The driver does not infer reader exit from a timeout, cancellation, result or renderer closure. At host exit it records outstanding sources, explicitly releases/cancels as necessary, observes bounded retirement and retains the result; any unresolved source remains outstanding/unqualified. Ordinary escaping callback/model exceptions retain the existing internal-error exit 4 with an inert frontend_event_error diagnostic and host cleanup and console/window cleanup, without manufacturing a successful renderer or storage result.
evidence: Retain initial/intermediate/final exact native captures, immutable publications, complete frame/context/reference values, actual worker code/process/request/epoch identities, model states at changed deliveries and final state before host teardown. Retain selected older frontend snapshots through later delivery and session destruction. Record callbacks/advance calls, zero controller storage/namespace/health dispatch, source outstanding/actual retirement, renderer exit, owned desktop/console observations and restored console modes/codepages/cursor/attributes. Independent fixtures define expected source coverage, stale focus and staged-review conflicts before evaluation.
limits: All existing source, worker/job, frame, graph/node, cached view/display/transcript and 256-MiB frontend process limits remain. The private driver and receipt bound their authored captures and retained test evidence; no production publication history chain or generic scheduler is added. Later live/provider/concurrent/public/durable/other-host/accessibility/writer/recovery/owner/release admission remains separate.
checks: Actual x64/Win32 owned GUI/TUI/linear-shell updates while injected native readers are pending; complete, partial/stale, denied, late/cancel/timeout and host-close ownership are tested at their stated scope.
Manual cached reads and automatic model delivery preserve exact original names, evidence selection and complete old native backing, without source control in getters or CompletionPoll.
Reviewed requests keep their source revision and conflict after replacement; editors/parameters/completion candidates remain exact, and shell target choosers cannot rebind by row index.
Exceptions, pending replacement refusal, finite deadlines and bounded explicit reader retirement preserve accurate failure/outstanding states and authority exclusions.
Existing frozen renderer, port/model and Fake product behaviors regress unchanged; retain exact source/toolchain/import/launch/host/evidence identities and partial implementer review.
Actual screen TUI cached updates across all three private observation compositions retain the exact old review and restore the caller buffer and console state.

Escaping pending-source application callback failures in GUI, linear/screen TUI and linear/screen shell retain internal-error 4, unavailable final model sample, separate actual reader retirement and complete old native backing.

Private deferred read-only completion remains bound to the exact original request/result through actual native observation delivery, with independent completion control, old-view/transcript retention and closure before completion without manufactured success.
private_host_selection: Optional terminal_style is exactly linear or screen and defaults to linear. Optional callback_fault is exactly none or pending and defaults to none. Invalid types/values are refused before opening readers. They are private fixture controls, never product flags or metadata-selected product composition.
screen_delivery_contract: An owned hidden console explicitly uses screen presentation at suitable geometry. Across metadata, full frame and compact identity captures, the TUI preserves its exact selected observation and staged target-inspect parameters/revision while a serialized application pulse delivers pending and later publications. The original review conflicts before health dispatch. On normal exit, original active buffer/content/cursor/viewport, modes, codepages, attributes and cursor style must be restored. Manual F5 refresh and operation CompletionPoll remain distinct from native reader control.
escaping_callback_contract: The private pending fault is thrown by the application callback after a pulse has prepared a changed publication with owned readers still outstanding; it escapes the driver error handler. GUI, linear/screen TUI and linear/screen shell must return internal-error 4 with only inert gui_event_error or frontend_event_error diagnostics. A successful/final model sample is unavailable on exceptional return; never call a captured model pointer after destruction. Record exact outstanding source state before the throw and independently at cleanup, explicit actual retirement, preserved old publications/native references after renderer and source-session destruction, and zero health/controller namespace/storage dispatch. A failed host does not establish reader exit or authorize replacement. Screen cleanup restores the original active buffer/content/cursor/viewport independently of any captured stderr diagnostic.
private_deferred_result: Optional deferred_completion is exactly none or inspect and defaults to none. inspect requires a separate completion_control string equal to the four validated source controls' same local nonce prefix plus .complete. none forbids that extra control. The completion event is opened only for SYNCHRONIZE and never interpreted as a source-control event. Combining inspect with pending callback_fault is a typed fixture conflict. Validate these selections before reader creation. No product flags or public endpoint.
deferred_result_semantics: At most one successful reviewed target.inspect result is computed against the exact original cached snapshot and withheld privately. Retain its full original completed envelope/parameters/revision/request identity and return the existing internal Submission::deferred() state. That queued submission is not a wire response or admitted operation: do not synthesize accepted_running or an operation identity. Deliver the exact original completed read-only envelope once only after the independent completion event. Its legitimately absent/null operation_id remains unchanged. This simulates deferred interface delivery, not asynchronous storage execution, a durable record, reconnect, freshness or authority.
completion_poll_boundary: CompletionPoll reads only its own owned zero-wait completion event and the precomputed pending response. It never calls native reader start/poll/release/cancel/timeout/retire, cached getters or application pulses. A source advance/release/cancel/timeout never consumes or acknowledges completion. A completion signal never replaces, retires or grants a reader. Existing four source event meanings and all native budgets remain.
deferred_delivery_contract: Submit the original review before starting a new capture. Actual GUI and linear/screen TUI retain the exact pending request while the changed native publication is delivered; the exact matching late completion clears pending and is retained separately from the current view. The actual linear shell keeps the original request/result transcript, old result basis and complete data while displaying its new cached view. No duplicate dispatch, ID/row rebinding, current-freshness or retry authority. Closure before completion retains an explicitly undelivered pending binding; host exit and native reader retirement remain separate. Normal screen-shell delivery, production asynchronous execution and durable reconnect remain separate work.
deferred_evidence: Retain the private queued-submission state and exact completed envelope, one original dispatch/completion count, full original result digest/basis, pending/final model states, native source/worker/epoch/code/process/frame/reference bindings, exact old publications after renderer/session teardown, actual owned GUI/console display and restoration. Required cases: changed native snapshot before independently released completion in GUI and linear/screen TUI and linear shell; closure while a withheld result remains pending. Validate the completed envelope against the current response contract; internal Submission state is not a response-schema instance. Keep all earlier 62-controller/113-reader journeys as regressions. This qualifies interface integration, not production operation execution.
completion_contract_refinement: Before implementation, inspection of runtime/presentation/requests.h established that frontend pending submission is distinct from a protocol accepted_running operation. This contract uses that existing boundary and creates no synthetic operation receipt.
